subject.title: Feature Request: Add .gitignore-like exclude patterns to backup CLI

question: Should OpenClaw add native backup exclude-pattern controls now, and what defaults, protected paths, and ignore-file behavior should become part of the core CLI contract?
rationale: The missing capability is clear, but the permanent behavior affects backup size, sensitive-file exposure, and whether restored archives remain complete enough to recover an installation.

options.title: Review linked PR as canonical
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/44288 to settle defaults, protected paths, manifest/JSON compatibility, proof, and any narrowing before landing or replacing it.

options.title: Ship explicit custom excludes first
options.body: Accept `--exclude` and `--exclude-file` only, while deferring smart defaults and auto-loaded ignore files until restore completeness and security expectations are clearer.

options.title: Decline native excludes for now
options.body: Keep built-in backups coarse, document current scope, and point optional backup strategies such as Keep My Claw to ClawHub until maintainers want a core contract.

recommendation.title: Review linked PR as canonical
recommendation.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/44288 to settle defaults, protected paths, manifest/JSON compatibility, proof, and any narrowing before landing or replacing it.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged/reviewed the original backup CLI contract and have the strongest history signal for deciding core CLI behavior boundaries.
